rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment tests the baseline performance of a simple RNA-only model with singleprofile and PCA encoding. This clarifies the impact of using RNA data alone and establishes a baseline for validation accuracy, helping isolate the effect of modality and encoding choices.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (RNA-only, singleprofile, PCA encoder) achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile (profile_setting=multiprofile) with avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation. It balances exploration (testing multiprofile) and exploitation (using the same RNA encoder and no image encoder). Multiprofile could capture more complex patterns, and avgpool is a simple aggregation method to assess its impact without introducing complexity from fusion or image encoders.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile (config_002) outperforms singleprofile (config_001) for RNA-only models. This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool (used in config_002) with transformer aggregation improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether transformer aggregation (a more complex method) could further enhance performance, balancing exploration of key design choices with exploitation of the promising multiprofile direction.

Existing evidence shows that for RNA-only models, multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (config_002) achieves higher accuracy (0.5907) than singleprofile or transformer aggregation. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (while keeping multiprofile and avgpool) improves performance, isolating the impact of the RNA encoder. This clarifies whether encoder choice is critical, leveraging the strong evidence from config_002 while exploring a key design decision.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 encoder with multiprofile and avgpool aggregation (config_005) achieves high validation accuracy (0.65). This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation (instead of avgpool) further improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It builds on the strong evidence for scvi_n200 and multiprofile, while exploring a key design choice with minimal changes.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder, multiprofile, and avgpool aggregation achieve the highest accuracy (0.653). This experiment tests adding image data (resnet50) to this strong baseline, isolating the effect of multimodal fusion. It directly addresses whether combining RNA and image modalities improves performance, a critical design choice with high potential impact.

Existing evidence shows that rna_only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy (0.653). This experiment tests whether combining this strong RNA encoder with multimodal data (resnet50 image encoder) and weighted fusion (vs. concat in config_030) can improve performance. It isolates the effect of fusion method in multimodal settings while reusing proven components, balancing exploitation of strong RNA encoder with exploration of multimodal potential.

Existing evidence shows that weighted fusion (config_033) and scvi_n200 RNA encoder (config_006) significantly improve performance. This experiment tests whether replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a larger, more complex image encoder) further enhances performance while keeping aggregation and fusion consistent. It isolates the impact of the image encoder, a critical component in multimodal models, and builds on the promising weighted fusion approach.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests whether replacing scvi_n200 with scgpt RNA encoder (a different representation) maintains or improves performance, isolating the impact of the RNA encoder choice. It balances exploration of new representations with leveraging prior success in multimodal setups.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_033: 0.713). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (while keeping other components fixed) improves performance, isolating the impact of the image encoder choice. This clarifies whether the image encoder's architecture significantly affects results, balancing exploitation of proven components with exploration of critical design decisions.
